extracted.intended_audience: users and developers of the PARI/GP system (mathematicians and programmers writing gp scripts and extensions)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for GP language constructs, control structures, runtime/debugging facilities, error types, and utility/library functions used when writing GP scripts or embedding PARI functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: dbg_up (dbg up({n = 1}))
rubrics_metrics.description: In the break loop, go up n frames to inspect data of the parent function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to view parent-function data while debugging. To cancel a dbg_up call, use dbg_down.

rubrics_metrics.name: dbg x (dbg x(A, {n}))
rubrics_metrics.description: Print the inner structure of A, complete if n is omitted, up to level n otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for debugging; similar to \x but does not require A to be a history entry. Can be used inside the break loop.

rubrics_metrics.name: for (for(X = a, b, seq))
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq with X going from a to b. Nothing is done if a > b. a and b must be in R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If b is +oo the loop does not stop (infinite loop expected); caller should break out with break or return. Example usage shown. Loop variable should not be modified in some specialized loops (see specific forxxx docs).

rubrics_metrics.name: forcomposite (forcomposite(n = a, {b}, seq))
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq where n ranges over composite numbers between real numbers a to b, inclusive if composite. Nothing is done if a > b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omitting b runs through all composites ≥ a (infinite loop expected). The value of n cannot be modified within seq; examples shown. Designed for iteration over composite integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: fordiv (fordiv(n = a, seq))
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq where X ranges through the divisors of n (or a factorization matrix). Assumes factor can handle n without negative exponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When n is integer, divisors are sorted by increasing size. To avoid storing all divisors, a slower constant-space routine using factorback is given. Examples compare performance with different approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: forell (forell(E, a, b, seq, {flag = 0}))
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterates E = [name, M, G] through all elliptic curves of conductors from a to b (name from Cremona database, M minimal model, G Z-basis of free part of E(Q)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag != 0, select only the first curve in each isogeny class. Requires elldata database installed for requested conductors. Counts and examples provided; library-level signature shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: forpart (forpart(X = k, seq, {a = k}, {n = k}))
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq over partitions X = [x1,...,xn] of integer k (nondecreasing parts). 0 has only empty partition; negatives have none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional parameters n (length restrictions) and a (part-size restrictions) are supported; behavior for filling zeros when amin ≤ 0 explained. The loop's behavior is unspecified if X is modified inside seq; examples shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: forprime (forprime(p = a, {b}, seq))
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq where p ranges over primes between real a and b inclusive. p is advanced to nextprime(p+1) each iteration. Nothing is done if a > b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting b to +oo produces an infinite loop. Value of p cannot be modified within seq (attempting to do so produces error). Examples shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: forstep (forstep(X = a, b, s, seq))
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq where X goes from a to b in increments of s. s must be in R* or a vector of step sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing done if s>0 and a>b or s<0 and a<b. If s is a vector [s1,...,sn], steps are used in order cyclically. b = +oo yields infinite loop unless broken.

rubrics_metrics.name: forsubgroup (forsubgroup(H = G, {bound}, seq))
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq for each subgroup H of the abelian group G (SNF form or vector of elementary divisors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If bound is integer, restrict to subgroups of index < bound; if bound is vector [B], restrict to index exactly B. Subgroups not ordered unless G is a p-group (Birkhoff's algorithm). Intended for huge groups where listing all subgroups is impractical. For canonical HNF printing use mathnf(concat(G,H)).

rubrics_metrics.name: forvec (forvec(X = v, seq, {flag = 0}))
rubrics_metrics.description: Let v be an n-component vector of [ai,bi] pairs; X ranges over the hyperrectangle with lexicographic ordering. X type matches v (t_VEC or t_COL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=1 generates only nondecreasing vectors; flag=2 only strictly increasing vectors. Examples illustrate ordering and flags.

rubrics_metrics.name: if (if(a, {seq1}, {seq2}))
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq1 if a is non-zero, otherwise seq2. seq1 or seq2 may be empty; special concise notations exist: if(a,seq), if(a,,seq) etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The if expression returns the value of the executed branch. Compound if constructs can encode switch/case via sequences of tests and branches. Boolean operators && and || short-circuit: evaluation of arguments stops as soon as truth value is determined (safe to use constructs like if(x != 0 && f(1/x), ...)). Note: break/next operate on loops; if is not a loop.

rubrics_metrics.name: iferr (iferr(seq1, E, seq2, {pred}))
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq1; on error sets formal parameter E to error data and, if pred absent or true, evaluates seq2 (which can reference E); otherwise rethrows error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: iferr returns seq2 when an error occurs, seq1 otherwise. Use to catch expected errors (e.g., in factoring algorithms); pred should check errname(E) or component(E,...) to discriminate error types. Examples given using iferr to implement resilient factoring (ECM) with explicit checks like errname(E)=='e_INV'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Error types overview (errname/structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The manual enumerates valid PARI error types (strings returned by errname(E)) and describes the contents/components of the attached error data E for each type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use errname(E) to obtain the error type string and component(E,i) to access attached data. The manual lists many error types with their component layout; these are used by iferr or by inspecting errors in debugging.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_ARCH
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_ARCH": Requested feature s is not available on this architecture/OS. E has one component (t_STR): feature name s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates platform limitations; useful to adjust feature usage or build.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_BUG
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_BUG": Bug in PARI library in function s. E has one component (t_STR): function name s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals an internal library bug; report to developers with context.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_FILE
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_FILE": Error while trying to open a file. E has two components: file type (t_STR) and file name (t_STR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occurs on I/O failures; check paths and permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_IMPL
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_IMPL": Requested feature s is not implemented. E has one component (t_STR): feature name s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature not yet implemented; adjust code or use alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_PACKAGE
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_PACKAGE": Missing optional package s. E has one component (t_STR): package name s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install or enable the package to access optional functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_DIM
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_DIM": Argument dimensions mismatch in function s (e.g., inconsistent matrix/vector sizes). E has three components: function name s, argument x, argument y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check argument dimensions passed to the function.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_FLAG
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_FLAG": A flag argument is out of bounds in function s. E has one component: function name s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate flags passed to functions against documented ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_NOTFUNC
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_NOTFUNC": Attempted function call on non-closure GEN x (e.g., f = 1; f(2);). E has one component: the offending GEN x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure callable objects are closures.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_OP
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_OP": Impossible operation between two objects that cannot be typecast to a sensible common domain for deeper reasons than type mismatch. E has three components: operator name op, first argument, second argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Occurs for e.g. O(2)+O(3) or incompatible p-adics; inspect operands and domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_TYPE
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_TYPE": An argument x of function s had an unexpected type. E has two components: function name s, offending argument x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate argument types per function contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_TYPE2
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_TYPE2": Forbidden operation between two objects that cannot be typecast to a common domain because their types do not match. E has three components: operator name op, first argument, second argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect types of operands; handle or convert appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_PRIORITY
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_PRIORITY": Object o in function s contains variables whose priority is incompatible with the expected operation (e.g., polynomial coefficients with higher-priority variables). E has four components: function name s, offending argument o, operator op describing priority error, variable v (t_POL) describing the priority error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid creating polynomials whose coefficients contain higher-priority variables than the main variable; adjust variable priorities or expression structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_VAR
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_VAR": Variables of arguments x and y submitted to function s do not match up (e.g., Mod(t,t^2+1) in nfinit(x^2+1)). E has three components: function name s, argument x (t_POL), argument y (t_POL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistent variable usage across arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_COMPONENT
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_COMPONENT": Accessing an inexistent component in vector/matrix/list (index out of bounds). E has four components: function name, operator op (< or >), numerical limit l (t_GEN), index x (GEN).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check indices and data sizes before access.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_DOMAIN
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_DOMAIN": Argument not in function's domain. E has five components: function name, mathematical name of out-of-domain argument, operator op describing domain error, numerical limit l describing domain error, out-of-domain argument x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate arguments against documented domain constraints (e.g., positive integers, ranges).

rubrics_metrics.name: e_MAXPRIME
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_MAXPRIME": Function using precomputed primes ran out of primes. E has one component: requested prime bound (t_INT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase prime limits or use methods that do not rely on precomputed prime lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_MEM
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_MEM": Memory allocation via pari_malloc or pari_realloc failed. E has no component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce memory use or increase available memory; consider optimizing algorithm or data structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_OVERFLOW
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_OVERFLOW": Object in function s becomes too large to be represented within PARI's hardcoded limits. E has one component: function name s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid extremely large exponentials or representations; rethink approach or use appropriate precision settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_PREC
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_PREC": Function s fails because input accuracy is too low (default accuracy). E has one component: function name s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase precision or provide higher-accuracy inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_STACK
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_STACK": The PARI stack overflows. E has no component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase stack via allocatemem/parisize(parisizemax), or restructure computation to use less stack (avoid deep recursion).

rubrics_metrics.name: e_ALARM
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_ALARM": A timeout generated by alarm; E has one component (t_STR) the error message to print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alarm to set execution timeouts; catch with iferr or adjust timeout.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_USER
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_USER": User error triggered by error(g1,...,gn). E has one component: the vector of n arguments given to error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raised intentionally by user code via error(); use for argument validation and aborting with messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_CONSTPOL
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_CONSTPOL": Argument of function s is a constant polynomial which does not make sense. E has one component: function name s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass non-constant polynomials when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_COPRIME
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_COPRIME": Function s expected coprime arguments but received x, y which were not. E has three components: function name s, argument x, argument y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure arguments are coprime when required or pre-process them.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_INV
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_INV": Tried to invert a non-invertible object x in function s. E has two components: function name s, the non-invertible x. If x = Mod(a,b) and a not 0 mod b, this can reveal a factor via gcd(a,b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check invertibility before inversion; use iferr to catch e_INV and possibly factor modulus (useful in factoring algorithms).

rubrics_metrics.name: e_IRREDPOL
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_IRREDPOL": Function s expected an irreducible polynomial but received T which was not. E has two components: function name s, the polynomial x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pass irreducible polynomials where required, or perform factorization/irreducibility checks first.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_MISC
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_MISC": Generic uncategorized error. E has one component: error message string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect error message for details; possibly rethrow or handle generically.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_MODULUS
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_MODULUS": Moduli x and y submitted to function s are inconsistent (e.g., mixing residue classes). E has three components: function s, argument x, argument y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistent modulus usage in modular arithmetic functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_PRIME
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_PRIME": Function s expected a prime number but received p which was not. E has two components: function name s, the argument p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate primality before calling functions that require primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_ROOTS0
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_ROOTS0": Argument of function s is the zero polynomial and roots are needed. E has one component: function name s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle zero-polynomial edge cases separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: e_SQRTN
rubrics_metrics.description: "e_SQRTN": Trying to compute an n-th root of x which does not exist in function s. E has two components: function name s, the argument x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check existence conditions or catch the error to handle non-existence cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: next ({n = 1})
rubrics_metrics.description: Interrupts execution of current seq and resumes the next iteration of the innermost enclosing loop (or n-th enclosing loop if n specified).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If n is bigger than the number of enclosing loops, all enclosing loops are exited. next operates only on loops.

rubrics_metrics.name: return ({x = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns from current subroutine with result x. If x omitted, returns no result (void) like print.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to exit functions with a value or void.

rubrics_metrics.name: until (until(a, seq))
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq until a is not equal to 0 (test after seq). If a initially non-zero, seq is evaluated once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semantics differ from while since condition tested post-execution (do-while behavior).

rubrics_metrics.name: while (while(a, seq))
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates seq while a is non-zero; test made before evaluating seq (pre-test loop). If a initially zero, seq is not evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard pre-condition loop semantics; use when possibly zero iterations are desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strprintf (Strprintf(fmt, {x}*))
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a string built from remaining arguments according to format fmt (formatting similar to printf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for building formatted strings; see printf for conversion specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: addhelp (addhelp(sym, str))
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes the help message for symbol sym to str (string expanded on the spot and stored as online help for sym).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended to document global variables and user functions. Attaching help to aliases has no visible effect because alias expansion shows help of the aliased symbol. Without addhelp, standard help shows name and definition; once addhelp used, function code is hidden from ?sym output but still accessible by typing the function name.

rubrics_metrics.name: alarm (alarm({s = 0}, {code}))
rubrics_metrics.description: If code omitted, trigger an e_ALARM exception after s seconds (cancels previous alarm). If code provided and s positive, evaluate code, aborting after s seconds returning a t_ERROR object on timeout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return value is code result if completed before timeout or a t_ERROR otherwise. Cannot set a new alarm inside an alarm code (new timer erases parent). Useful to bound execution time; example shows using alarm to attempt factoring and fallback to partial factorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: alias (alias(newsym, sym))
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines newsym as an alias for sym. Works for ordinary functions, member functions (prefix '.'), and operators (use internal operator names).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aliases are expanded at compile-time, affecting only GP code compiled after alias evaluated. For dynamic behavior, use variables; examples show pitfalls (aliases don't change past compiled definitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: allocatemem (allocatemem({s = 0}))
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes GP stack size after initialization. If s>0, allocate new stack of at least s bytes; if s=0, double current stack size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavior depends on parisizemax default: with parisizemax enabled there are virtual stack size (parisizemax), desired typical size (parisize), and current stack size (can be changed). With parisizemax disabled (deprecated default), allocatemem acts like default(parisize, ...). Changing stack in some contexts interrupts current computation (longjmp) and discards remaining sequences; allocatemem cannot be used meaningfully inside loops or as part of larger expressions. Use in interactive/breakloop contexts to reduce garbage collection. Examples and caveats provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: apply (apply(f, A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply closure f to entries of A: if A scalar return f(A); if polynomial/power series apply to coefficients; if vector/list return elements f(x); if matrix return matrix of f(A[i,j]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many functions are componentwise on vectors/matrices but not lists; apply is useful for lists. List comprehension/set notation shortcuts available: [g(x) | x <- v, f(x)] and others that translate to apply/select idioms. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: call (call(f, A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given vector A = [a1,...,an] and function f, returns f(a1,...,an). If #A = 1, call(f,A) = apply(f,A)[1]. Variadic arguments must be grouped in a vector in the last component of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for writing variadic wrappers and for calling functions with runtime-determined arity. Examples include fprintf/write wrappers and memoization implementation. Library-level signature noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: default (default({key}, {val}))
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the default corresponding to keyword key; if val present sets default to val first (subject to string expansion). default() (or \d) yields complete default list and values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See sections for list of available defaults and interactive shortcuts. Library-level function default0 available.

rubrics_metrics.name: errname (errname(E))
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns the type of error message E as a string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use with iferr to discriminate errors by type and inspect component(E,i) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: error (error({str}*))
rubrics_metrics.description: Outputs its arguments (interpreted as strings) then interrupts running gp program, returning to input prompt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to raise user errors with informative messages, e.g., error("n = ", n, " is not squarefree!").

rubrics_metrics.name: extern (extern(str))
rubrics_metrics.description: Runs an external shell command str and feeds its output into gp as if read from a file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to import command output directly into GP interactive/session input.

rubrics_metrics.name: externstr (externstr(str))
rubrics_metrics.description: Runs an external shell command str and returns its output as a vector of GP strings, one element per output line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for programmatically capturing external command output without feeding into GP input stream.

rubrics_metrics.name: fold (fold(f, A))
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply closure f of arity 2 to entries of A in a left-fold manner, returning f(...f(f(A[1],A[2]),A[3])...,A[#A]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include product, nested pairing, function composition application, and rational transformation examples. Library-level genfold variants noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: getabstime (getabstime())
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns CPU time (ms) elapsed since gp startup (reentrant version of gettime).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for measuring CPU-time elapsed in code segments reliably across calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: getenv (getenv(s))
rubrics_metrics.description: Return value of environment variable s if defined, otherwise 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to configure GP behavior based on environment; library-level gp_getenv available.

rubrics_metrics.name: getheap (getheap())
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns two-component row vector: number of objects on heap and amount of memory they occupy (in long words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primarily for debugging memory usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: getrand (getrand())
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns current value of the seed used by pseudo-random generator random. Technical internal state only usable with setrand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for reproducing sequences for debugging; returned value is internal state representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: getstack (getstack())
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns current value top - avma, i.e., number of bytes used so far on the stack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for debugging stack usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: gettime (gettime())
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns CPU time (ms) used since last call to gettime or since beginning of containing GP instruction, whichever later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reentrant CPU timing use getabstime; for wall-clock use getwalltime.

rubrics_metrics.name: getwalltime (getwalltime())
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns time (ms) elapsed since UNIX Epoch (wall-clock time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to measure wall-clock durations; example shows difference usage with getabstime/gettime.

rubrics_metrics.name: global (global(listof variables))
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete; scheduled for deletion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use; maintained only for backwards compatibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: inline (inline(x, ..., z))
rubrics_metrics.description: (Experimental) Declare x,...,z as inline variables: behave like lexically scoped variables but with unlimited scope; can exit scope with uninline().
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When used in GP scripts, call uninline() before script end to avoid leaking inline variables outside script.

rubrics_metrics.name: input (input())
rubrics_metrics.description: Reads a string interpreted as GP expression from input file (usually stdin). If sequence of expressions given, returns result of last expression in sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using pari.el under Emacs, must prompt the user with a prompt string ending with same prompt as previous ones. Use print1 to prompt the user in interactive scripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: install (install(name, code, {gpname}, {lib}))
rubrics_metrics.description: Loads from dynamic library lib the function name and assigns it the name gpname in current gp session with prototype code. Gives access to non-static functions defined in PARI library and to external functions in linked shared libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prototype encoding: first char for return type (i,l,v default GEN), letters for argument types (G,&,L,s,n), p/P for precision, and DG/D&/Dn for optional args. Re-install warns and updates prototype but does not reload library symbol. Caution: may segfault on statically linked gp on first use. Examples: installing addii to expose low-level int addition, or installing system-like functions. Library-level gpinstall available.

rubrics_metrics.name: kill (kill(sym))
rubrics_metrics.description: Restores symbol sym to its 'undefined' status and deletes any help messages attached via addhelp. Does not remove variable names from interpreter (name still known).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Killing a user function does not remove its name from variable list. To reset variables to starting values without deleting help, use quote operator (a = 'a). kill is the only way to remove aliases and installed functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: listcreate (listcreate({n}))
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete; creates an empty list. Use List instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kept for backward compatibility; prior mandatory argument ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: listinsert (listinsert(L, x, n))
rubrics_metrics.description: Inserts object x at position n in list L (type t_LIST). Complexity O(#L - n + 1) due to shifting elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when needing ordered insertion into lists; for appending prefer listput or list[n] = x.

rubrics_metrics.name: listkill (listkill(L))
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete; retained for backward compatibility. Use L = List() instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local variables are automatically cleared when user function returns; explicit listkill usually unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: listpop (listpop(list, {n}))
rubrics_metrics.description: Removes the n-th element of list (t_LIST). If n omitted or > length removes last element. If list empty, do nothing. Runs in O(#L - n + 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to remove elements; note complexity for large lists when removing near front.

rubrics_metrics.name: listput (listput(list, x, {n}))
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets n-th element of list (t_LIST) to x. If n omitted or greater than length, appends x. Returns the inserted element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simpler than manual shifting; examples show appending behavior and returning inserted value. Standard list[n]=x syntax is more natural in many cases.
